title: The Joy and Pain of Training an LLM from Scratch
excerpt: Alessandro Ercolani documents the full pipeline behind the Zagreus and Nesso small language model families, from framework selection with Nanotron through tokenizer data engineering and Slurm-driven pretraining to multilingual evaluation, with honest notes on what broke along the way.
author: Alessandro Ercolani
coverAlt: Zagreus and Nesso training report cover

title: Techniques for Training Large Neural Networks
excerpt: OpenAI walks through the parallelism toolbox for training large models, explaining how data, pipeline, tensor, and expert parallelism each split computation across GPUs, where the communication costs land, and which memory-saving tricks make the pieces fit.
author: Lilian Weng and Justin Jay Wang

title: Dolma: 3 Trillion Token Open Corpus for Language Model Pretraining
excerpt: Ai2 explains how it assembled Dolma, a 3-trillion-token openly licensed pretraining corpus, walking through source selection, language and quality filtering, deduplication, and toxicity decisions, and releases the toolkit so the pipeline can be audited or remixed.
author: Luca Soldaini

title: Introducing the Third Generation of Apple's Foundation Models
excerpt: Apple details its third-generation foundation model family: a 3B dense on-device model, a 20B sparse on-device model that activates only 1-4B parameters per request, and three server models on Private Cloud Compute, with privacy-preserving deployment as a first-class design constraint.
author: Apple Machine Learning Research
coverAlt: Apple Foundation Models third generation hero image

title: Accelerating Gemma 4: Faster Inference with Multi-Token Prediction Drafters
excerpt: Google engineers explain how Multi-Token Prediction drafters give Gemma 4 up to a 3x decoding speedup through a specialized speculative decoding architecture, covering why standard LLM inference is memory-bandwidth bound and how draft-and-verify preserves output quality.
author: Olivier Lacombe and Maarten Grootendorst

title: Structured State Spaces: Combining Continuous-Time, Recurrent, and Convolutional Models
excerpt: Albert Gu, Karan Goel, and Chris Re unpack the S4 architecture, showing how one state space model can be computed as a continuous-time system, a recurrence, or a convolution, and why switching between the three views unlocks efficient long-range sequence modeling.
author: Albert Gu, Karan Goel, and Chris Re
coverAlt: State space model diagram from the S4 blog

title: Learning to Reason with LLMs
excerpt: OpenAI describes how o1 was trained with large-scale reinforcement learning to produce a private chain of thought before answering, and shows accuracy climbing smoothly with both train-time and test-time compute across competition math, coding, and science benchmarks.
author: OpenAI

title: MaxProof: Scaling Mathematical Proof with Generative-Verifier RL and Evolutionary Search
excerpt: MiniMax details the framework that pushed its M3 model past the human gold-medal threshold on IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026, combining a stronger base prover, an aligned generative verifier, refinement training, and evolutionary search at test time.
author: MiniMax

title: The Illustrated Retrieval Transformer
excerpt: Jay Alammar visualizes DeepMind's RETRO, explaining step by step how a 7.5B-parameter model backed by a trillion-token retrieval database can match far larger models by separating world-knowledge lookup from language modeling.
author: Jay Alammar

title: The Illustrated Transformer
excerpt: The canonical visual walkthrough of the Transformer, building up self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, and the encoder-decoder stack one diagram at a time - still the fastest way to develop intuition for the architecture behind modern LLMs.
author: Jay Alammar

title: Mapping the Mind of a Large Language Model
excerpt: Anthropic reports the first detailed look inside a production LLM, using sparse autoencoders to extract millions of interpretable features from Claude 3 Sonnet - including safety-relevant ones - and showing that amplifying or suppressing features causally changes behavior.
author: Anthropic
coverAlt: Vintage head diagrams representing concept mapping inside an AI model

title: Language Models Perform Reasoning via Chain of Thought
excerpt: Jason Wei and Denny Zhou show that simply prompting large models to produce intermediate reasoning steps unlocks major gains on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning - and that chain-of-thought ability emerges only past a certain model scale.
author: Jason Wei and Denny Zhou
coverAlt: Chain-of-thought prompting illustration from Google Research

title: What's Going On with the Open LLM Leaderboard?
excerpt: Hugging Face's evaluation team dissects why three implementations of the same MMLU benchmark give wildly different LLaMA scores, tracing the gaps to prompt formatting and log-likelihood versus generation-based scoring - a cautionary tale for anyone comparing eval numbers.
author: Clementine Fourrier, Nathan Habib, Julien Launay, and Thomas Wolf
coverAlt: Open LLM Leaderboard MMLU deep dive cover

title: Illustrating Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)
excerpt: Nathan Lambert and collaborators break RLHF into its three trainable stages - a base language model, a human-preference reward model, and PPO-based policy optimization - clarifying what each stage actually optimizes and where the open research problems sit.
author: Nathan Lambert, Louis Castricato, Leandro von Werra, and Alex Havrilla

title: Demystifying Multimodal Learning: Enabling Vision in Language Models
excerpt: Matteo Nulli builds vision-language models up from first principles: the mathematical formulation, ViT-CLIP vision encoders, contrastive alignment of image and text embeddings, and the architectural flow that turns raw pixels into tokens an LLM can attend to.
author: Matteo Nulli
coverAlt: VLM architecture overview from the demystifying multimodal learning post

title: Generalized Visual Language Models
excerpt: Lilian Weng surveys four families of visually-augmented language models - joint training on image-text pairs, learned visual prefixes, cross-attention fusion, and frozen-LLM approaches - comparing how each injects vision into a text backbone and what it costs.
author: Lilian Weng
coverAlt: VisualBERT architecture diagram from Generalized Visual Language Models

title: Multimodality and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs)
excerpt: Chip Huyen maps the large multimodal model landscape, working through CLIP's contrastive pretraining and Flamingo's vision-language fusion in detail, then cataloging the data, architecture, and training choices that separate today's LMM systems.
author: Chip Huyen
coverAlt: CLIP architecture diagram from the LMM overview

title: Accelerating Document AI
excerpt: Rajiv Shah, Niels Rogge, and Nicholas Broad organize document AI into six practical use cases - from OCR and classification to layout analysis, document QA, and table extraction - matching each with open-source models like LayoutLM and Donut and the licensing realities practitioners face.
author: Rajiv Shah, Niels Rogge, and Nicholas Broad
